evidence_items.explanation: The study demonstrates real failures of safeguards in multiple models. It does not measure benign-request refusals or establish that every guardrail lacked a practical balance.

XSTest found GPT-4 fully refused 6.4% and partially refused 2% of safe prompts, while refusing all but one of 200 unsafe prompts. This challenges a sweeping failure claim, but the unsafe contrasts were not a comprehensive adversarial safety evaluation.

The paper reports substantial defense against GCG attacks while retaining useful performance. Its PAIR test still had an attack success rate around 50%, and general question-answering performance is not a direct measure of inappropriate refusal.

unresolved_gaps: No sufficiently comprehensive evaluation establishes the universal assertion across guardrails available by the post.
The sources do not establish a shared practical threshold for acceptable refusal and attack-success rates.
Positive results have limited test coverage; demonstrated failures do not themselves establish that all balances were ineffective.
